hook: Pay as much attention to the document as to the creature it describes. It is by qntm, an author well known on the wiki for antimemetic stories, and the loss of memory and information is again at its centre. The later paragraphs get harder to read; do not skim them.
whyItMatters:
SCP-2256 is a compact demonstration of antimemetics: something that resists being perceived or remembered. Where many antimemetic entries frame the idea as a threat, this one turns it into an ecological tragedy and a question about the ethics of research.

It shows that the format can carry grief just as well as fear.
thingsToNotice:
The black bars here are not routine redaction. Watch them spread through the History section until whole sentences break apart. The procedures warned that detailed records decay fastest, so the entry you are reading is itself rotting in front of you.

Meanwhile the central dilemma, that watching the species may be what doomed it, is raised and never settled, which works as a quiet indictment. The islanders' myth, in which the creatures guard the horizon, is a small touch that makes the loss feel larger.

related.note: Another file that seems eaten away by the phenomenon it documents.
A classic antimeme, about what cannot be known rather than what is lost.
